findings.title: Describe lists non-food extraFoods that Build silently drops
findings.detail: TitanDiet.Build only keeps an extraFoods entry if it is nutrition-giving, or if it isn't food and has nutrition > 0. Anything else is skipped (the `else if (f.nutrition > 0f)` branch around Source/TitanDiet.cs:68). Describe adds every non-null f.thing to the 'Also eats:' line (around Source/TitanDiet.cs:117-122). So a trait def that lists, say, steel without a nutrition value shows 'Also eats: steel' in the hediff tooltip, but the creature never eats it, and the info card's Diet line (from ExtraFoodsLabel, built off Build's sets) leaves it out. Use the same check in Describe: `if (f.thing != null && (f.thing.IsNutritionGivingIngestible || f.nutrition > 0f))`.

findings.title: Card Diet value leaves out refused foods and hunting
findings.detail: The rebuilt Diet entry shows Apply(race) plus ExtraFoodsLabel, so a known trait's refuseFoods and its hunts setting never appear on the info card. Only the hediff tooltip shows them. The behaviour is correct; whether the card should mention them is a design choice.

findings.title: TradeSession reordering applies Trade mode to every pawn valued while Dialog_Trade is open
findings.detail: Trade mode is now checked first and requires Dialog_Trade to be open. That fixes the stale TradeSession.trader case (the vanilla corpus has no TradeSession.Close() call, so the comment is right). But any market-value request made while the dialog is open, including for pawns not in the trade, still gets the mystery bonus. That was already true before this change, so it's not a regression.
